summary: RAM Law (Rebenack Aronow & Mascolo LLP) is a plaintiff-side personal injury litigation firm founded in January 2007, with offices in New Brunswick, Somerville and Manalapan, NJ. It markets itself on 11 certified civil trial attorneys, rare truck-accident board certification and more than $170M recovered in ten years, and runs bilingual (English/Spanish) marketing with 24/7 phone intake and office hours to 8pm on weekdays. Case volume is coordination-heavy: multi-office intake, medical-bill organization, records collection and insurance negotiation all sit on top of a website tracked by call-tracking and lead-routing tools.

facts.fact: Firm was opened in January 2007 by three founding partners (Ed Rebenack, Craig Aronow, Jay Mascolo) who previously practiced at the largest law firm in New Brunswick; it now includes associates, counsel attorneys and paralegal staff.

Firm states it has 11 certified civil trial attorneys and that two of its attorneys are board-certified in truck accident law by the National Board of Trial Advocacy, which it says is 50% of all such attorneys in New Jersey.
Firm advertises $170+ million in compensation recovered in 10 years and $80+ million for survivors of childhood sexual abuse.
Three offices are listed: 111 Livingston Avenue, New Brunswick NJ 08901; 21 North Bridge Street, Somerville NJ 08876; and 348 Route 9, Suite E, Manalapan NJ 07726.
Practice areas listed include truck accidents, car accidents, construction site accidents, pedestrian accidents, childhood sexual abuse, slip/trip and falls, dog bites and defective products/drugs.
Manalapan office page lists office hours of Monday–Friday 8:00 AM–8:00 PM, Saturday and Sunday closed, and 'Phone Intake Hours 24/7'.
Main published number is (732) 247-3600 with a single shared email contact@ram.law for all three offices; the New Brunswick location page also displays a second number, 848-280-7810.
Firm partner Edward J. Rebenack lists a direct line and email on his profile; he is described as Co-Founder and Partner with 29 years in practice, and obtained a Class A CDL permit in 2018.
On-site review display shows a 4.8 rating based on 72 reviews for 'Rebenack Aronow & Mascolo L.L.P.'
Careers page invites applicants generally ('always on the lookout for talented individuals') but lists no specific open positions and asks recruitment agencies not to submit resumes.
A SimplyHired search for RAM Law jobs in New Brunswick, NJ returned zero results.
Elyssa A. Goldstein (CLM, PHR, SHRM-CP) is listed as Chief Operating Officer of Rebenack, Aronow & Mascolo, LLP; she began in legal as a receptionist in 2009 and moved into legal management in 2013.
Kanika J. Malhotra is listed as Marketing Director, responsible for marketing, brand strategy and community engagement.
The site is bilingual: a full Spanish-language version exists under /es/ and Spanish-language articles appear in the blog feed.

Recent results highlighted on the site include a $30,000,000 verdict against the City of Newark and Newark Board of Education in a sexual abuse case and a $25,000,000 verdict in the first Child Victims Act trial against the State of New Jersey.

operations_signals: Two intake channels are promoted on every page: 'contact us online' (web form) and phone at (732) 247-3600; there is no online scheduling or client portal link (https://ramlawnj.com/contact/).

Phone intake is advertised as 24/7 while office hours are Monday–Friday 8:00 AM–8:00 PM and closed weekends, implying after-hours calls are answered by something other than office staff (answering service or intake vendor) (https://ramlawnj.com/manalapan-new-jersey/).
Extended weekday hours to 8:00 PM plus weekend closure is consistent with evening-heavy consumer intake (https://ramlawnj.com/manalapan-new-jersey/).

The firm publishes a numbered list of what it does for truck crash clients that includes organizing medical bills, handling insurance company interactions, managing property damage claims, identifying medical specialists and investigating the accident scene — all labor-intensive, document- and phone-driven tasks (https://ramlawnj.com/).

One shared email address (contact@ram.law) serves all three offices, with separate fax numbers for New Brunswick and Somerville, so inbound inquiries are not routed by location at first contact (https://ramlawnj.com/contact/).

Service area is described as Middlesex, Somerset and Monmouth counties, with clients traveling between the New Brunswick, Somerville and Manalapan offices (https://ramlawnj.com/manalapan-new-jersey/).
Firm works on contingency ('no fees unless we win'), which makes case screening and intake qualification an economic choke point (https://ramlawnj.com/the-firm/).
hiring_signals: No open positions are listed on the firm's careers page; it carries only a standing invitation to apply and a note refusing unsolicited recruiter submissions (https://ramlawnj.com/careers/).

A SimplyHired search for RAM Law jobs in New Brunswick, NJ returned '0' results, suggesting no active public postings at the time of research (https://www.simplyhired.com/search?q=RAM+Law&l=New+Brunswick%2C+NJ).

The only two non-attorney profiles published in the site's staff directory are the COO and the Marketing Director — roles that point to operations/HR and marketing rather than to case-processing staff (https://ramlawnj.com/staff-profile/elyssa-goldstein/).

Team composition described on the site is 'associates, counsel attorneys, and paralegal staff' with no separate intake, records or billing roles named, so those functions appear to be absorbed by paralegals and support staff (https://ramlawnj.com/attorney-profile/).
review_themes: Testimonials the firm publishes emphasize responsiveness and organization — clients describe staff replying quickly, returning calls and emails, and keeping them updated (https://ramlawnj.com/what-our-clients-say/).

Referral sources are a recurring theme: one reviewer describes being an attorney who sends civil cases to the firm, and another says they refer everyone they know to a named partner (https://ramlawnj.com/what-our-clients-say/).
Client comments repeatedly name individual attorneys and paralegals, implying that personal availability of staff is part of the value proposition (https://ramlawnj.com/what-our-clients-say/).

The on-site review module shows 4.8 stars over 72 reviews, and all testimonials displayed are 5-star; no negative or mixed reviews are shown on the site, so complaints cannot be assessed from firm-published material (https://ramlawnj.com/what-our-clients-say/).
tech_footprint: WordPress site built with Elementor and Yoast SEO, running WPML multilingual plugin with a full Spanish translation of pages, posts and staff bios (https://ramlawnj.com/).
Forms are Gravity Forms; every page funnels to a web contact form rather than a scheduling calendar (https://ramlawnj.com/).

CallRail call tracking is installed, which explains multiple displayed numbers ((732) 247-3600, 848-280-7810, plus a direct partner line) and implies per-channel/per-office call attribution (https://ramlawnj.com/).
A Lawbrokr script is loaded and initialized on the homepage — a legal-specific intake/lead widget product (https://ramlawnj.com/).
A Juvo Leads tag is installed, indicating paid lead purchasing or lead routing alongside owned intake (https://ramlawnj.com/).

Advertising and analytics stack includes Google Tag Manager, GA4/UA, a Google Ads conversion tag (AW-17361478205), Bing UET, Outbrain pixel and an OpenAI Ads base pixel, showing heavy paid-acquisition instrumentation (https://ramlawnj.com/).
The firm publishes a frequently updated blog mixing New Jersey accident news and legal explainers, in English and Spanish (https://ramlawnj.com/blog/).
No visible client portal, case-status lookup, live chat or payment page was found on the site; engagement is phone/form first (https://ramlawnj.com/contact/).
growth_signals: Firm markets three offices across three counties and describes itself as serving clients throughout central New Jersey from New Brunswick, Somerville and Manalapan (https://ramlawnj.com/).

Result announcements are frequent and large: a $30M verdict against Newark and its school board, a $25M verdict in the first Child Victims Act trial, and a $19.5M child sexual abuse settlement, among dozens of others (https://ramlawnj.com/).

National Board of Trial Advocacy truck-accident certification (2019 for Rebenack) plus a Class A CDL permit and truck-driving school are used to differentiate the truck-crash practice, a growth niche (https://ramlawnj.com/attorney-profile/edward-j-rebenack/).
Partner Craig Aronow was named 2025 Civil Trial Practice Attorney of the Year by the Middlesex County Bar Association (https://ramlawnj.com/somerville-new-jersey/).

The firm added marketing and operations leadership roles — a Marketing Director and a COO with HR certifications — which typically accompanies expansion of headcount and office footprint (https://ramlawnj.com/staff-profile/kanika-j-malhotra/).
Blog content is being published on a near-weekly cadence in late 2026, including Spanish-language posts, indicating continued investment in organic intake (https://ramlawnj.com/blog/).
decision_maker: Edward J. Rebenack, Co-Founder and Partner (operations led by Elyssa A. Goldstein, Chief Operating Officer), listed on the firm's own site — https://ramlawnj.com/attorney-profile/edward-j-rebenack/ and https://ramlawnj.com/staff-profile/elyssa-goldstein/

inferences.inference: Intake is staffed by a mix of in-house personnel and an outside answering/intake service rather than by the website alone.
inferences.reasoning: The firm advertises 24/7 phone intake but 8am–8pm weekday office hours and closed weekends, and it runs both a Lawbrokr intake widget and a Juvo Leads tag, which are typically paired with after-hours call handling.

inferences.inference: Case-file administration is likely a bottleneck: medical-bill organization, records requests to providers, and insurer follow-up are described as firm responsibilities and scale linearly with case count.
inferences.reasoning: The firm explicitly lists organizing medical bills and managing insurer interactions as services, and it advertises 11 trial attorneys plus a large verdict/settlement volume across three offices without naming dedicated records or billing staff.

inferences.inference: Marketing spend is channel-fragmented and measured per call, which creates reporting and follow-up reconciliation work.
inferences.reasoning: CallRail dynamic number insertion, multiple tracking numbers, Google Ads conversion tags, Bing UET, Outbrain and an OpenAI ads pixel are all present on the same page, so leads arrive from several paid channels that must be matched to intakes.

inferences.inference: The firm likely has a modest total headcount (roughly two to three dozen people) rather than a large-firm structure.
inferences.reasoning: Eleven attorneys plus associates/counsel, two published non-attorney leadership profiles (COO, Marketing Director) and paralegal staff suggest a mid-sized boutique, though no headcount is published.

inferences.inference: Spanish-language demand is treated as a core market, not an afterthought.
inferences.reasoning: The entire site is translated via WPML, Spanish blog posts are published alongside English ones, and the firm advertises a bilingual attorney on staff.

inferences.inference: No hiring is visibly underway, so staffing strain would show up as workload on existing paralegals rather than as open requisitions.
inferences.reasoning: The careers page lists no roles, SimplyHired shows zero postings, and the site's staff directory contains only two support-side profiles.

data_gaps: No job postings could be verified: Indeed, LinkedIn Jobs and ZipRecruiter returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches; SimplyHired was the only job board that loaded and showed zero results.

Independent review platforms (Google Business Profile, Yelp, BBB, Avvo) could not be retrieved — access was blocked — so review themes rely on the firm's curated on-site testimonials and its 4.8/72 widget.
Office hours are published only for the Manalapan location; New Brunswick and Somerville hours are not stated on their pages.
No information found on which case management, document management, e-signature or billing software the firm uses internally.
No published headcount, revenue, case-volume counts or intake-volume metrics.
No indication of how after-hours calls are handled (in-house staff, answering service or vendor) beyond the '24/7 phone intake' claim.
Local news coverage (expansions, office openings, awards outside the firm's own site) could not be searched because web search providers were unavailable during this session.
